Started with focused probes to observe object lifecycles and APIs, then implemented ARIS Script (Java SE6 + JavaScript hybrid) reports and macros. Prioritized small, testable scripts and safe deployment patterns (checks and fallbacks) to avoid disruptions.
Designed small experiments to safely observe runtime behavior and iterated until script behavior was predictable.
Delivered report scripts that extract process data, format it for business consumption, and export in required formats.
Built macros that let business users run routine operations without needing deep developer involvement.

Keeping disparate enterprise systems in sync with a pragmatic, reusable approach

I split the problem into three practical layers: small, reusable service clients; a transformation engine driven by a simple Expr-based configuration; and an orchestration layer that runs and monitors pipelines. Each piece is versioned and tested independently so teams can add a connector without touching everything else.
Delivered a SuccessFactors ↔ ARIS sync that reduced stale data windows from hours to minutes. It runs as a Kubernetes cron job and tolerates transient failures.

Migrated services gradually to TypeScript and the new architecture to avoid big-bang rewrites and reduce downtime.

Rebuilding old JDE workflows as practical, data-heavy web apps

I built React + TypeScript frontends backed by a Java + Spring Boot API. Delivered configurable grids with dynamic columns, fast filtering, and sensible pagination so users can actually work with 10k+ rows without endless scrolling.
Implemented CSV/Excel/PDF exports that preserve formatting and calculated fields so downstream reports no longer need manual fixes.
Used gRPC where it mattered to reduce request times for large, repeated queries—users noticed the difference during day-to-day tasks.

Migrated features from the XML-based UI to the web apps without breaking workflows; the product teams could swap components incrementally.

I rewrote the service in Kotlin with Spring Boot and Kotlin Exposed. I focused on small, testable modules and a hexagonal structure so the core logic lives alone and adapters do the dirty work. That made tests simpler, database changes safer, and future refactors less scary.

Ogni componente ha versioning e test indipendenti, così si può aggiungere un connector senza toccare il resto.
Conseguita la sincronizzazione SuccessFactors ↔ ARIS che ha ridotto il delay da ore a minuti. Il job gira come cron su Kubernetes e resiste a errori transitori.
Creato un formato di mapping basato su Expr: i product manager possono modificare regole senza deploy; supporta campi calcolati e condizioni.
Implementate librerie Go per NetSuite, ARIS e il PIM interno: partire da codice funzionante è molto più veloce che ricominciare da zero.
